question: Explain how the energy band gap helps in distinguishing metals, semiconductors and insulators. Give reason for the difference in their electrical conductivity.

options.A:
Metals
They have a large energy band gap, so electrons are unable to move freely.
Semiconductors
They have no band gap and therefore conduct like metals.
Insulators
They have overlapping valence and conduction bands, so their conductivity is highest.
options.B:
Metals
The valence band and conduction band overlap, or the conduction band is partially filled, so many free electrons are available and conductivity is high.
Semiconductors
They have a small forbidden energy gap, so some electrons gain thermal energy to reach the conduction band and conductivity is moderate.
Insulators
They have a large forbidden energy gap, so electrons cannot easily reach the conduction band and conductivity is very low.
options.C:
Metals
They have a small but finite band gap, so their conductivity is lower than semiconductors.
Semiconductors
They have a large band gap and no free charge carriers at room temperature.
Insulators
They have partially filled conduction bands, so they conduct easily.
options.D:
Metals
They have no electrons in the conduction band, so conductivity is low.
Semiconductors
They have the largest energy gap and therefore highest conductivity.
Insulators
They have the smallest energy gap, so electrons move freely.
